# Requirements Readiness Checklist: Reference Data Lookup by Type and ID

**Purpose**: Full pre-implementation requirements-quality review — validates that `spec.md` is complete, clear, consistent, measurable, and traceable before `/speckit-implement` begins. This checklist tests the requirements as written, not the eventual implementation.
**Created**: 2026-09-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the field set returned for types with no additional fields (e.g. `genders`, `appointment_titles`) explicitly distinguished from types with extra fields, rather than left to inference from the Key Entities description? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the response body shape for the 400/401/404 error cases specified within `spec.md` itself, rather than only referenced indirectly via the Assumptions bullet on a "shared, project-wide error body shape"? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for how `attribute_name` casing is handled (e.g. a request for `Jurisdictions` instead of `jurisdictions`)? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK004 Is there a requirement describing behavior if a lookup is attempted before the reference-data set has finished loading at startup? [Completeness, Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "invalid credentials" (as distinct from "missing" credentials) defined concretely enough to determine what request shape counts as each, or left to reader interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, User Story 1 Scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "well-formed identifier" (FR-008) defined precisely enough to determine whether a negative number, a decimal, or a number with leading zeros counts as well-formed or malformed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "a known, valid combination of attribute type and record ID" (User Story 1) defined precisely enough to distinguish a legitimately-held identifier from an arbitrary guessed number that happens to exist in the dataset? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 1]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Do FR-006 (unknown ID) and FR-007 (unknown type) specify whether their "not found" responses must be distinguishable from each other, or does SC-003's grouping of both into one "unknown type or ID" outcome leave that intentionally unspecified? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK009 Does "invalid credentials" in FR-009 stay consistent with the Assumptions bullet stating authentication is simulated (not a real identity check), or could a reader interpret FR-009 as requiring real credential validation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK010 Does FR-005's guarantee that a lookup "MUST NOT return records from any other type" read as consistent with the Key Entities description of records holding cross-type IDs (e.g. `jurisdiction_id`), or could a reader see a conflict between "no other type's data" and "contains another type's ID"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §Key Entities]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Is SC-002's "zero behavioural difference" backed by an objective comparison standard (e.g. byte-for-byte identical body), or could "identical result" be read as merely semantically equivalent? [Measurability, Ambiguity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK012 Is SC-004's "well under one second" quantified with a specific numeric threshold, or left as a qualitative target open to interpretation? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK013 Can SC-003's claim that four outcome classes are reliably distinguishable "with no overlap" be verified directly from the functional requirements, or does it depend on error-body details not yet specified in `spec.md` (see CHK002)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Are concurrent-request scenarios (e.g. two clients requesting the same type/ID at once) addressed in requirements, or only single-request behavior? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK015 Is there a requirement for what happens if the same deprecated alias could ever resolve to more than one canonical type, or is this explicitly excluded as impossible by the Key Entities' one-to-one alias mapping? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK016 Are retry/idempotency expectations addressed for a caller that receives a 401 and retries with corrected credentials? [Coverage, Gap]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Beyond the five documented Edge Cases, is there a requirement for a `reference_id` value that is numeric but exceeds any reasonable/expected magnitude (e.g. far larger than any real dataset ID)? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the behavior for an empty-string `attribute_name` (as opposed to an entirely absent path segment, covered by FR-004) explicitly distinguished from an unsupported-but-non-empty type name? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-004, §FR-007]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK019 Are logging requirements defined for what MUST NOT be logged on an authentication failure (e.g. the raw credential value), given the Assumptions bullet on shared, project-wide observability? [Non-Functional, Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the correlation/trace identifier's role scoped clearly as an operational/debugging aid rather than a client-facing contract element consumers must parse or act on? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK021 Is the assumption that the source specification's documented `attribute_name` list is "complete and matches the available seed data" validated against anything, or only asserted? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the dependency on the dated seed-data snapshot (`joh-elinks-api/ReferenceData/`, filenames embedding `2026-06-01`) remaining stable/unreplaced documented as an assumption, given the feature's correctness examples (e.g. `jurisdictions/30` → "Courts") are tied to that snapshot? [Assumption, Gap]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK023 Do the two Assumptions bullets introduced for project-wide observability/error-shape governance describe business-observable behavior (what a consumer sees), or do they read as implementation detail that belongs in `plan.md` rather than `spec.md`, given this template's "avoid HOW, focus on WHAT" guidance? [Scope, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK024 Is it clear from `spec.md` alone whether the correlation identifier is guaranteed present on every response, including ones the client did not request one for, or could a reader infer it only applies to error responses? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
